activity.title: As I get ready to begin my journey as a Materials Science and Engineering student at UC Berkeley, I’ve been reflecting on one of the experiences that made me feel like I truly belonged at Cal. This summer, I had the opportunity to participate in the UC Berkeley Pre-Engineering Program (PREP), where I spent three weeks learning, building, and connecting with an amazing community of students and mentors. One of the highlights of the program was our capstone project. Working with my team, I got hands-on experience taking an idea from the drawing board to a working prototype. I had the opportunity to work with Arduino, CAD, 3D printing, and soldering while developing our project and learning what it takes to collaborate and problem solve as an engineer. We also had the opportunity to present our project and receive feedback from professionals from organizations including NVIDIA, BlackRock, and the California Department of Technology. Being able to share our work with industry professionals was an incredible experience and gave me a glimpse into the kind of work and collaboration I hope to pursue throughout my time at Berkeley. I’m incredibly grateful Marvin J. Lopez , Britt Mazorra , our mentors, and everyone who helped make PREP such a memorable experience. I’m excited to take everything I learned both inside and outside the classroom into this next chapter. Thank you for welcoming me into the Berkeley community. Go Bears! 🐻 ...more

UC Berkeley has been named the top public university in the U.S., and No. 7 globally in U.S. News & World Report’s 2026 Best Global Universities rankings. The rankings also assess a university’s strength in various subject areas. This year, Berkeley was named in the top five globally in a number of subjects, including physics (No. 3), biology and biochemistry (No. 4), economics and business (No. 4), environment/ecology (No. 4), and space science (No. 5). The best global university list is distinct from the U.S. News & World Report ranking of the best American colleges and universities, which is calculated using different metrics and released each September. Berkeley also claimed the top public institution slot on the latter list in 2025. More on UC Berkeley News: https://lnkd.in/ggPPRjCd #UCBerkeley #Cal #USWNR ...more ...more

This week, SMASH Scholars joined the National Football League (NFL) Inspire Change Super Bowl STEAM Celebration in San Francisco as part of Super Bowl LX week, alongside members of the SMASH leadership team. Through hands-on learning experiences and conversations with NFL players, mentors, and leaders, high school scholars explored how science, technology, engineering, arts, and math connect to real-world opportunities and future careers. SMASH CEO Jonathan Durfield was also on site, connecting with partners including NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, reinforcing the importance of visibility and partnership in spaces where innovation and leadership intersect. As SMASH marks 25 years of impact, moments like this highlight the power of sustained collaboration. This summer, I had the honor of being one of the first Chemical Engineers to participate in the PREP Pre-Engineering Program at UC Berkeley alongside George Santiago Luna and Estefani Esther Esqueda Galvez . PREP is a three-week summer intensive program that guides incoming engineers by focusing on three main topics: the academic rigor at UC Berkeley, product development through CAD and 3D printing to solve a real-world problem, and the fundamentals of networking and professionalism. I would like to thank my team members, Sergio Carrillo Martinez , Marvin Gregory Singleton , Isabella Rosas , and Esmeralda Martinez, for their dedication, hard work, and inclusiveness throughout the program. I hope to be able to continue being someone they can count on throughout the next four years at UC Berkeley. I would also like to thank Britt Mazorra and Marvin J. Lopez for including College of Chemistry engineering students and planning such a wonderful program that gives us first-year students "a leg up" as we approach our first year at Berkeley. I am grateful for the many speakers who were able to give us insight into different aspects of engineering and student life at Berkeley, including David Yee , whose story of resilience and perseverance inspires me to push forward during times of hardship. And finally, a special thank you to my calculus teacher, Galilea Gonzalez , for teaching me how to approach the rigors of UC Berkeley math and sharing her insights into different study habits and strategies that led to her success. I would also like to thank my dormitory floor's Resident Assistant, William Lopez Rodas , who created a welcoming environment and shared his background and accomplishments, inspiring me to strive for similar success during my next four years at Cal. The memories made during this program are unforgettable, and I am looking forward to seeing the 2026 PREP Cohort again in the fall! Go Bears! 🐻

first generation filipina from sfv going to berkeley engineering 😍👏👏🤪🤪 wait… FIRST gen FILIPINA from SFV…. going to BERKELEY ENGINEERING 😟😰😰 This past March, I opened my laptop to discover my acceptance to UC Berkeley. Initially, I had trouble accepting this merit, and my jubilation was (slightly) inhibited by intimidation: how am I going to survive at the #1 public university & #3 engineering program in the world? ?!!?!!!! However, I later received more great news that I was accepted into the Pre-Engineering Program (PREP), for which I’ve had the privilege and pleasure to participate in a 3-week intensive, developing my academic and professional skills to acclimate to the UC Berkeley rigor. The summit of my experience occurred on July 31st: the Maker Design Expo. In just ~26 hours of instructional time, I gained hands-on experience in Arduino, CAD, C++, and 3D printing to develop Nexus: a wearable fall-detection device designed to aid users while reducing medical costs. That day, my team — Ubah Ismail , Pedro Terrero Chavez , Jefferson Martinez , Barbara Avalos , and I — proudly engineered and presented our prototype. I’d like to express my appreciation for Scott Moura and Sebastian Castañeda Guerrero for leading us through the Maker Design Studio. Your wisdom and dedication are a huge inspiration. A special ‘thank you’ to our Design Assistant, Alan Romero . Your advocacy and encouragement fostered our success! I am honored to be part of a program of such outstanding individuals, as each student in my cohort feels like family. A special thanks to the Learning Fascilitator, Galilea Gonzalez : your compassionate guidance has given me the self-assurance to thrive academically. Additionally, a huge ‘thank you’ to the Residential Assistants, Estela Jauregui Jauregui and William Lopez Rodas , for your kind mentorship and support as leaders in PREP. You all made this summer incredibly memorable. Ultimately, I am sincerely grateful to Marvin J. Lopez & Britt Mazorra for organizing this program. This opportunity has allowed me to find my community, my belonging, and my home at Berkeley. 🐻💛 (& shout out to jude BELLINGHAM) #FirstGeneration #WomenInSTEM #UCBerkeley #SanFernandoValley

TPREP 2026 is officially in the books! Over the past three weeks in UC Berkeley’s Transfer Pre-Engineering Program, I pushed my academic and professional limits alongside an inspiring community of CoE staff, mentors, and peers. I spent my mornings diving back into Linear Algebra and Computer Science refreshers to prepare for the rigor of EE 66 and CS 61A, learning how to embrace the challenge and build academic resilience for the semester ahead. In my afternoons, I was at the Jacobs Institute of Design Innovation with my team, Dust Busters! Guided by Claire Beaudin , we tackled indoor air quality for respiratory health by building SPOT✅, a device that alerts homeowners of unseen dust buildup in hard-to-reach places. As Head of Electronics, I integrated a Pixy2 camera, RGB LED, and LCD screen. Challenges with our build occurred when our LCD screen wasn't responding to our programmer's code. However, our Design Assistant, Edmond Ter-Pogosyan , helped us pivot, ultimately combining the LCD and RGB LED into a dual alert output system. From brainstorming, after-hours team meetings, and soldering in the Makerspace, I couldn't have asked for a better experience. I'm truly honored to have had the opportunity to work on SPOT✅ alongside the Dust Buster team. I will definitely use my upgraded skills in CAD, soldering, circuits, and product development to spearhead my next project. As a first-generation Latina in Engineering, TPREP was a surreal milestone. The people I met in and out of the program have been the highlight of my last three weeks, and I cannot wait to begin my first semester at Berkeley alongside them. I sincerely want to thank Monica Marquez , Marvin J. Lopez , David Yee , the TPREP staff, and my cohort for making this program an unforgettable first-time experience as a UC Berkeley engineer. GO BEARS! 🧸 💙💛

I got into Jane Street twice in one summer. Last May, I attended their FOCUS program, and soon, I’ll be heading back for a longer stay as part of the SWE track with Jane Street’s INSIGHT program! Coming in, I knew almost nothing about quantitative trading. I left thinking about it completely differently. During FOCUS I got a real look at the daily lives of Jane Street's engineers. The firm builds nearly its entire stack in OCaml, a functional language most of the industry has barely touched. Engineering and trading are woven together in a way I hadn't seen before, where the people writing the code are right next to the markets it moves. But the biggest thing I took away wasn't technical. It was the conversations, with engineers about how they think through problems, with peers who pushed me to think harder about my own path. I learned more in that short window than I expected to about a field I barely understood going in. That's when I knew I had to go back. INSIGHT is my chance to go deeper: into the stack, the culture, and the kind of engineer I want to become. Special thanks to Kylie Newman & Katie Nasta for organizing FOCUS and making my experience possible.

Last Friday, as an incoming civil engineering student, I had the opportunity to attend the Pre-Engineering Program (PREP) Expo at UC Berkeley, where my team and I got the chance to present our project! Throughout the three-week program leading up to the Expo, I was introduced to Berkeley’s course rigor through calculus and chemistry classes taught by our student teachers, Ernesto De Santiago and Galilea Gonzalez . Not only did I gain a sense of what it would be like to attend classes at Berkeley, but I also got the chance to become familiar with the campus, staff, and welcoming community! To bring our final project design to life, we completed the SPRINT project process led by Scott Moura and Sebastian Castañeda Guerrero , with the help of our DA, Mariela Hernandez Delgado . My teammates, Irvin Angeles , Crystal Echeverria, Valeria Castillo, Sebastian Latham , and I came up with the idea of a portable translator that would be small enough to fit on a keychain. Although our prototype was not the ideal size, we created a demo and design that we hope to develop further in the future! We were given approximately 26 hours to put together our prototype and presentation, making it such an unforgettable experience and one that I learned so much from! Along with working on our project, we also attended workshops led by Marvin J. Lopez , David Yee , and others, where we learned about career paths, time management, and the programs and resources available to us on campus. I am so grateful for this program, as it has helped prepare me for my time at UC Berkeley! This experience has taught me the importance of teamwork, strengthened my networking and leadership skills, and introduced me to so many amazing individuals. Thank you to Britt Mazorra , my RA Yulia Yang , and everyone I had the opportunity to connect with throughout these three weeks! I can’t wait to officially attend Berkeley and continue growing within its community! Go Bears!! 💙🐻

I’m so excited to share that I’ve completed UC Berkeley’s PREP program for incoming engineers! Over the past few weeks, I’ve had the opportunity to experience different aspects of what it means to be an engineer. Through coursework in computer science and calculus, I strengthened my academic foundation while also developing professional skills that will help me as I begin my journey as a Berkeley engineer. One of the most influential parts of this program was our three week Design Lab, where my team identified and focused on the challenge of elderly fall recovery. We explored the difficulties older adults can face when trying to get back up after a fall and designed/prototyped a walker with extending legs to help make the recovery process safer and more accessible. After three weeks of researching, designing, and iterating on our idea, we presented our solution at a final expo. I walk away from this experience not only as a stronger engineer, but a stronger person. It has showed me how engineering combines technical knowledge, creativity, and collaboration to address real-world problems. I’m grateful for everything I learned, the people I met, and the opportunity to challenge myself in a new, fast-paced environment. I’m excited to take these experiences with me into the next chapter at UC Berkeley and continue growing as an engineer. Go Bears! 🐻💙💛

Last Friday, the UC Berkeley Pre-Engineering Program came to an end, and I couldn't have asked a better way to have had spent three weeks out of my summer. I had the upmost privilege to meet some of the most amazing and ambitious people during these three weeks. They supported me throughout the program, and I hope I can grow with them for the next four years that are to come at the University of California, Berkeley. The PREP Expo was also an amazing experience as I got a to work in a team where we had to create a project in small amount of time. I am beyond proud of the work my team and I accomplished. It was truly fascinating seeing nothing turn into something. Last but not least, I want to give a huge thank you to Marvin J. Lopez and Britt Mazorra for making PREP what it was. I learned and experienced so many new things that I would've pictured. I will always carry all the skills and lessons I have learned with me, always remembering, “what got you here, won't get you there". GO BEARS! 🐻 #UCBerkeley #Engineering

My journey with UC Berkeley Pre-Engineering Program (PREP) came full circle this summer. After participating as a student in the PREP class of 2025, I was honored to return to the program as a Residential Assistant for the incoming class of 2026. This transition allowed me to contribute to a community that has been foundational to my own engineering career. PREP is an intensive three-week program designed to support first-generation college students by providing them with a robust professional network and introducing them to the vast resources within UC Berkeley Engineering. A cornerstone of the experience is the SPRINT project design competition. During this competition, students develop essential technical skills—including programming, CAD, and prototyping—to create functional solutions for real-world problems, which they eventually present to a panel of judges. Serving as a Residential Assistant, I worked alongside William Lopez Rodas , Yulia Yang , Joaquin Cabrera Caballero , and Floormate Milagros Perez Mejia to support our students within the residential halls. Over the course of the program, I witnessed a remarkable transformation as the students acclimated to the Berkeley lifestyle and grew into confident, driven individuals. It was a privilege to mentor the PREP cohort of 2026 and observe their professional and personal development firsthand. I would like to extend my sincere gratitude to my supervisors, Britt Mazorra and Marvin J. Lopez , for their leadership in hosting such a successful program. I am also grateful to everyone who supports PREP, ensuring it continues to provide vital opportunities for aspiring engineers. Finally, congratulations to the PREP class of 2026 on taking this significant first step into Berkeley Engineering. Go Bears!

I am extremely excited and grateful to share that I have officially completed the three week Pre-Engineering Program (PREP) at UC Berkeley! As my transition to UC Berkeley approached, I was nervous about finding my community, adjusting to the academic rigor, and simply knowing my way around campus. PREP not only reduced my stress, but also transformed it into excitement for my freshman year. From attending professionalism workshops, to preparing for my upcoming fall courses, to creating endless memories with my fellow “PREPies,” my eagerness to begin my academic journey at UC Berkeley grew every day. Being surrounded by caring faculty and driven and like-minded students made finding community feel natural. I would like to sincerely thank Marvin J. Lopez and Britt Mazorra for organizing such an amazing program. They gave me the platform to strengthen my resume, elevator pitch, and professional presence, while even providing us with professional headshots. Additionally, I am grateful to David Yee , whose story taught me that resilience is key to fostering not only success at Berkeley, but in life. I have a special appreciation for Galilea Gonzalez , who proved to be one of the most resourceful and caring instructors I have ever had. Recognizing my advanced placement in mathematics, she shared resources that will allow me to independently prepare for Math 53 during the school year. I would also like to thank Ernesto De Santiago for his daily chemistry lectures. Thanks to both of them, I am entering the fall semester academically prepared. Furthermore, my dormitory floor’s residential assistant, William Lopez Rodas , played a major role in making this program so special. Hearing about his background and personal experiences at UC Berkeley allowed me to “reverse-engineer” his path and envision how I can build similar success. Now, as I transition to UC Berkeley as an incoming Chemical Engineering student, I have a clearer understanding of my career goals, how I will approach academic rigor, and where to turn for support. I will forever cherish the lessons, memories, and friendships I gained through the 2026 PREP cohort. Go Bears! 🐻💙💛
